title: Farm Stay Holidays Booming in the UK
paragraphs: What do you imagine when you picture the perfect holiday location? A luxury hotel? A lounge chair by a pool?
Holiday stays on farms — or "farmcations" — are now booming in the UK, with young people especially attracted by country breaks with fresh air, birdsong and locally grown food.
Recent data from Airbnb shows that farm stay bookings in the UK went up by 14% this summer compared to last summer. And among younger people aged between 18 and 28, farm stay bookings went up by 41%!

For farmers, the "agritourism" industry provides a useful income stream. Working farms are increasingly converting old farm buildings into holiday cottages, adding glamping tents to their properties and offering experiences like collecting eggs, cooking, gardening and farm animal tours.

Caitlin Owens, owner of Fowlescomb Farm in Devon, told Condé Nast Traveller that visitors enjoy being part of the working life of the farm. "Even if only for a night or two, guests can come and connect to the farm; the people who work here, the dogs, the sheep in the fields and the chickens next to the orchards," she said.

Many farms also offer wellness retreats. Louma in West Dorset, for example, has converted its barn into a wellness center with swimming pools, a sauna and a gym. Yoga and Pilates classes and massage treatments are also available.

Freshly cooked, home-grown seasonal food is another big part of the attraction of farmcations. At the Knepp Estate in West Sussex, visitors can learn how to grow their own food in gardening workshops, and eat meat and vegetables grown at Knepp in the farm's own restaurant.

The Knepp Estate is also the home of a very successful rewilding project that has returned much of the farm to a more natural state that is able to support more wildlife. The farm offers safari tours to view wild horses, deer and many rare birds.
